tokyo_kyoeido.price_note: ⚠ THE MOST USEFUL SINGLE SENTENCE FOUND IN THIS ENTIRE DATASET, AND THE SHOP VOLUNTEERS IT: 「当店独特の濃褐色のソースは、小麦粉を一切使わず、20数種類の香辛料を1時間かけてじっくり炒めて作ります」 — the curry sauce uses NO WHEAT FLOUR AT ALL, none, and is built instead on twenty-odd spices fried for an hour and vegetables cooked down until they disappear. Japanese curry is the most reliable wheat trap in the country because カレールー is a flour-and-fat roux sold as a brick; this 1924 shop makes its curry the Indonesian way and says so on its own site, unprompted, as a point of pride about texture rather than as an allergen claim. That is a first-party statement about the exact ingredient a coeliac needs, and it makes the four plain curries here the best hot main in the Tokyo set. ⚠ AND THE SAME PAGE, THREE LINES LOWER, TAKES IT BACK FOR THE REST OF THE PLATE. Under Soup: 「野菜と小麦を数回オーブンにかけルーを作り、コーン・生クリームを合わせた」 — the soup that accompanies the curry is a ROUX made from vegetables and WHEAT, finished with cream. So the shop removes flour from the thing everyone assumes has it, and puts flour into the thing nobody thinks to ask about. Order the curry, refuse the soup. ⚠ TWO ITEMS RE-INTRODUCE THE FLOUR BY A DIFFERENT DOOR: タンカレー has デミグラスソース added to the curry sauce, and ハヤシライス is built on the shop’s 特製デミグラスソース outright. A demi-glace is a browned flour roux by definition and the shop makes no flour-free claim for it — so of six mains, four are on the flour-free sauce and two are not. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. 神田神保町; 11:00–20:00 (L.O. 19:45), closed Sundays and public holidays; founded 大正13年 (1924), the recipe learned from 伊藤友治郎 and adapted to Japanese taste. Rice is 国産コシヒカリ.

⚠ THE TRAP, IN THE SHOP’S OWN WORDS: 「野菜と小麦を数回オーブンにかけルーを作り、コーン・生クリームを合わせた」 — vegetables and WHEAT baked into a roux, then corn and CREAM. The one component of this meal that is made of flour is the one served alongside a curry that is not. No price is published for it separately.

tokyo_beppinsha.price_note: PARTIAL: dish names and descriptions from the shop’s own menu page, which prints NO PRICES — every price field below is empty rather than guessed. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE SHOP BRANDS ITSELF "Gluten Free Spice Curry" ON ITS OWN SITE HEADER, which is a claim worth taking seriously and worth reading carefully. A spice curry is built on whole and ground spices, onion and stock rather than on a カレールー brick, so a flour-free curry is entirely achievable and this kitchen advertises it as its identity — the same territory as スマトラカレー共栄堂 elsewhere in this set, which states 小麦粉を一切使わず outright. ⚠ BUT THE SITE STOPS AT THE HEADER. The menu page describes each curry’s spices, heat level and contents and does NOT repeat the gluten-free claim per dish, does not name a flour substitute, and publishes no allergen statement, no cross-contamination note and nothing about the kitchen. So the flags below are "ask" and not "gf": the branding is a strong lead and it is not an ingredient declaration, and this dataset does not upgrade on branding. It is a very good shop to ring ahead to. ⚠ AND THE DRINKS LIST UNDOES IT ANYWAY: the shop pours 志賀高原ビール — Shiga Kogen pale ale and IPA — and BEER IS BARLEY MALT. A gluten-free curry house with a craft beer list is a real combination, and the beer is the wheat-and-barley item on the premises. Heat is chosen from 1 to 6 on most curries.

tokyo_lavoro.price_note: ⚠ THIS IS THE ONLINE SHOP, NOT A RESTAURANT BOARD — the stored website is a BASE storefront selling whole and sliced cakes for delivery. No in-store menu or price was found. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ AND IT IS A USEFUL COUNTER-EXAMPLE TO THE RICE-FLOUR ASSUMPTION. Every product here declares 卵・米粉・乳: egg, RICE FLOUR and dairy. So the flour is rice — which means the cakes are very likely wheat-free and would suit a coeliac — while the egg and milk make them firmly not vegan. That is the mirror image of the pattern this dataset usually records, where a dish is plant-based and full of wheat. 米粉 on a Japanese label is a signal about GLUTEN and says nothing whatsoever about animal ingredients, and the two are constantly conflated by shops and customers alike. ⚠ THE FLAGS ARE "ask" ON GLUTEN RATHER THAN "gf" for one reason: the shop lists rice flour as an ingredient but makes no gluten-free CLAIM, publishes no statement about its kitchen, and a bakery that uses rice flour is not the same thing as a bakery with no wheat in it — contrast BIOSSA elsewhere in this set, which states 「完全」グルテンフリー and 28品目不使用 outright. ⚠ ONE ITEM CARRIES A NUT: モンコーネ contains アーモンドパウダー. Several cut sizes were sold out at the time of reading and are recorded with their listed prices anyway.
